1.1: Then Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab:
1.2: And Ahaziah fell thorow the lattesse window in his upper chamber which was in Samaria: so he was sick: then he sent messengers, to whom he said, Goe, and enquire of Baal-zebub the God of Ekron, if I shall recover of this my disease.
1.3: Then the Angel of the Lord said to Eliiah the Tishbite, Arise, and goe up to meet the messengers of the King of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is no God in Israel, that ye goe to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?
1.4: Wherefore thus saith the Lord, Thou shalt not come down from the bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt die the death. So Eliiah departed.
1.5: And the messengers returned unto him, to whom he said, Why are ye now returned?
1.6: And they answered him, There came a man and met us, and said unto us, Goe, and return unto the King which sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Is it not because there is no God in Israel, that thou sendest to enquire of Baal-zebub the God of Ekron? Therefore thou shalt not come down from the bed, on which thou art gone up, but shalt die ye death.
1.7: And he said unto them, What maner of man was he which came and met you, and told you these wordes?
1.8: And they said unto him, He was an hearie man, and girded with a girdle of lether about his loynes. Then sayde he, It is Eliiah the Tishbite.
1.9: Therefore the King sent unto him a captain over fiftie with his fiftie men, who went up unto him: for behold, he sat on the toppe of a mountain, and he said unto him, O man of God, the King hath commanded that thou come down.
1.10: But Eliiah answered, and said to the captain over the fiftie, If that I be a man of God, let fire come down from the heaven, and deuoure thee and thy fiftie. So fire came down from the heaven and deuoured him and his fiftie.
1.11: Again also he sent unto him another captain over fiftie, with his fiftie. Who spake, and said unto him, O man of God, thus the King commandeth, Come down quickely.
1.12: But Eliiah answered, and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from the heaven, and deuoure thee and thy fiftie. So fire came down from the heaven, and deuoured him and his fiftie.
1.13: Yet again he sent the third captain over fiftie with his fiftie. And the third captain over fiftie went up, and came, and fell on his knees before Eliiah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life and the life of these thy fiftie servants be precious in thy sight.
1.14: Behold, there came fire down from the heaven and deuoured the two former captaines over fiftie with their fifties: therefore let my life now be precious in thy sight.
1.15: And the Angel of the Lord said unto Eliiah, Goe down with him, be not afraid of his presence. So he arose, and went down with him unto the King.
1.16: And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast sent messengers to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, (was it not because there was no God in Israel to inquire of his word?) therefore thou shalt not come down off the bed, on which thou art gone up, but shalt die the death.
1.17: So he dyed according to the word of the Lord which Eliiah had spoken. And Jehoram began to reign in his stead, in the second yeere of Jehoram the sonne of Jehoshaphat King of Judah, because he had no sonne.
1.18: Concerning the rest of the actes of Ahaziah, that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

2.1: And when the Lord would take up Eliiah into heaven by a whirle wind, Eliiah went with Elisha from Gilgal.
2.2: Then Eliiah said to Elisha, Tarie here, I pray thee: for the Lord hath sent me to Bethel. But Elisha said, As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came down to Beth-el.
2.3: And the children of the Prophets that were at Beth-el, came out to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the Lord will take thy master from thine head this day? And he said, Yea, I know it: hold ye your peace.
2.4: Again Eliiah said unto him, Elisha, tarie here, I pray thee: for the Lord hath sent me to Jericho: But he said, As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came to Jericho.
2.5: And the children of the Prophets that were at Jericho, came to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou, that the Lord will take thy master from thine head this day? And he sayde, Yea, I know it: hold ye your peace.
2.6: Moreover Eliiah said unto him, Tarie, I pray thee, here: for the Lord hath sent me to Iorden. But he said, As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they went both together.
2.7: And fiftie men of the sonnes of the Prophets went and stood on the other side a far off, and they two stood by Iorden.
2.8: Then Eliiah took his cloke, and wrapt it together, and smote the waters, and they were deuided hither and thither, and they twain went over on the dry land.
2.9: Now when they were passed over, Eliiah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall doe for thee before I be taken from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let thy Spirit be double upon me.
2.10: And he said, Thou hast asked an hard thing: yet if thou see me when I am taken from thee, thou shalt have it so: and if not, it shall not be.
2.11: And as they went walking and talking, behold, there appeared a charet of fire, and horses of fire, and did separate them twain. So Eliiah went up by a whirle wind into heaven.
2.12: And Elisha saw it, and he cryed, My father, my father, the charet of Israel, and the horsemen thereof: and he saw him no more: and he took his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces.
2.13: He took up also the cloke of Eliiah that fell from him, and returned, and stood by the bank of Iorden.
2.14: After, he took the cloke of Eliiah, that fell from him, and smote the waters, and sayde, Where is the Lord God of Eliiah? And so he also, after he had striken the waters, so that they were deuided this way and that way, went over, even Elisha.
2.15: And when the children of the Prophets, which were at Jericho, saw him on the other side, they sayde, The Spirit of Eliiah doeth rest on Elisha: and they came to meet him, and fell to the ground before him,
2.16: And said unto him, Behold now, there be with thy servants fiftie strong men: let them go, we pray thee, and seek thy master, if so be the Spirit of the Lord hath taken him up, and cast him upon some mountain, or into some valley. But he said, Ye shall not send.
2.17: Yet they were instant upon him, til he was ashamed: wherefore he said, Send. So they sent fiftie men, which sought three dayes, but found him not.
2.18: Therefore they returned to him, (for he taryed at Jericho) and he said unto them, Did not I say unto you, Goe not?
2.19: And the men of the citie said unto Elisha, Behold, we pray thee: the situation of this citie is pleasant, as thou, my lord, seest, but the water is naught, and the ground baren.
2.20: Then he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.
2.21: And he went unto the spring of the waters, and cast there the salt, and said, Thus saith the Lord, I have healed this water: death shall no more come thereof, neither barennesse to the ground.
2.22: So the waters were healed until this day, according to the word of Elisha which hee had spoken.
2.23: And he went up from thence unto Beth-el. And as he was going up the way, litle children came out of the citie, and mocked him, and said unto him, Come up, thou bald head, come up, thou bald head.
2.24: And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. And two beares came out of the forest, and tare in pieces two and fourtie children of them.
2.25: So he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.

3.1: Now Jehoram the sonne of Ahab beganne to reign over Israel in Samaria, the eighteenth yeere of Jehoshaphat King of Judah, and reigned twelve yeeres.
3.2: And he wrought evil in the sight of the Lord, but not like his father nor like his mother: for he took away the image of Baal that his father had made.
3.3: Nevertheless, he cleaved unto the sinnes of Jeroboam, the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne, and departed not therefrom.
3.4: Then Mesha King of Moab had store of sheep, and rendred unto the King of Israel an hundreth thousand lambes, and an hundreth thousand rammes with the wool.
3.5: But when Ahab was dead, the king of Moab rebelled against the King of Israel.
3.6: Therefore King Jehoram went out of Samaria the same season, and nombred all Israel,
3.7: And went, and sent to Jehoshaphat King of Judah, saying, The King of Moab hath rebelled against me: wilt thou goe with me to battell against Moab? And he answered, I will goe up: for I am, as thou art, my people, as thy people, and mine horses as thine horses.
3.8: Then said he, What way shall we goe up? And he answered, The way of the wilderness of Edom.
3.9: So went the King of Israel and the king of Judah, and the King of Edom, and when they had compassed the way seven dayes, they had no water for the host, nor for the cattell that followed them.
3.10: Therefore the King of Israel sayde, Alas, that the Lord hath called these three Kings, to give them into the hand of Moab.
3.11: But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a Prophet of the Lord, that we may inquire of the Lord by him? And one of the King of Israels servants answered, and said, Here is Elisha the sonne of Shaphat, which powred water on the handes of Eliiah.
3.12: Then Jehoshaphat said, The word of the Lord is with him. Therefore the King of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, and the King of Edom went down to him.
3.13: And Elisha sayde unto the King of Israel, What have I to doe with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father and to the prophets of thy mother. And the King of Israel said unto him, Nay: for the Lord hath called these three Kings, to give them into the hand of Moab.
3.14: Then Elisha said, As the Lord of hostes liveth, in whose sight I stand, if it were not, that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the King of Judah, I would not have looked toward thee, nor seen thee.
3.15: But now bring me a minstrel. And when the minstrel played, the hand of the Lord came upon him.
3.16: And he said, Thus saith the Lord, Make this valley full of ditches.
3.17: For thus saith the Lord, Ye shall neither see wind nor see rain, yet the valley shalbe filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye and your cattel, and your beastes.
3.18: But this is a small thing in the sight of the Lord: for he will give Moab into your hand.
3.19: And ye shall smite every strong town and every chief citie, and shall fell every fair tree, and shall stoppe all the fountaines of water, and marre every good field with stones.
3.20: And in the morning whe the meat offring was offred, behold, there came water by the way of Edom: and the countrey was filled with water.
3.21: And when al the Moabites heard that the Kings were come up to fight against them, they gathered all that was able to put on harness, and vpwarde, and stood in their border.
3.22: And they rose earely in the morning, when the sunne arose upon the water, and the Moabites saw the water over against them, as red as blood.
3.23: And they said, This is blood the Kings are surely slain, and one hath smitten another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoyle.
3.24: And when they came to the host of Israel, the Israelites arose up, and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them, but they invaded them, and smote Moab.
3.25: And they destroyed the cities: and on all the good field every man cast his stone, and filled them and they stopt all the fountaines of water, and felled all the good trees: onely in Kirharaseth left they the stones thereof: howebeit they went about it with slings, and smote it.
3.26: And when the King of Moab saw that the battel was too sore for him, he took with him seven hudreth men that drew the sword, to break through unto the King of Edom: but they could not.
3.27: Then he took his eldest sonne, that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him for a burnt offring upon the wall: so that Israel was sore grieved, and they departed from him, and returned to their countrey.

4.1: And one of the wives of the sonnes of the Prophets cryed unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant mine husband is dead, and thou knowest, that thy servant did fear the Lord: and the creditour is come to take my two sonnes to bee his bondmen.
4.2: Then Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell mee, what hast thou at home? And she sayd, Thine handmayd hath nothing at home, save a pitcher of oyle.
4.3: And he sayde, Goe, and borowe thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, emptie vessels, and spare not.
4.4: And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sonnes, and powre out into all those vessels, and set aside those that are full.
4.5: So she departed from him, and shut the door upon her, and upon her sonnes. And they brought to her, and she powred out.
4.6: And when the vessels were full, she sayde unto her sonne, Bring mee yet a vessel. And hee said unto her, There is no moe vessels. And the oyle ceased.
4.7: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Goe, and sell the oyle, and pay them that thou art in debt unto, and live thou and thy children of the rest.
4.8: And on a time Elisha came to Shunem, and there a woman of great estimation constrained him to eat bread: and as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.
4.9: And she sayde unto her husband, Behold, I know now, that this is an holy man of God that passeth by us continually.
4.10: Let us make him a litle chamber, I pray thee, with walles, and let us set him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick, that hee may turn in thither when hee cometh to us.
4.11: And on a day, hee came thither and turned into the chamber, and lay therein,
4.12: And sayd to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite: and when hee called her, she stood before him.
4.13: Then he sayd unto him, Say unto her now, Behold, thou hast had all this great care for us, what shall we doe for thee? Is there any thing to bee spoken for thee to the King or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among mine own people.
4.14: Again he sayde, What is then to be done for her? Then Gehazi answered, In deed she hath no sonne, and her husband is old.
4.15: Then said he, Cal her. And hee called her, and she stood in the door.
4.16: And he said, At this time appointed, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a sonne. And she sayd, Oh my Lord, thou man of God, doe not lye unto thine handmayd.
4.17: So the woman conceived, and bare a sonne at that same season, according to the time of life, that Elisha had sayd unto her.
4.18: And when the child was growen, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father, and to the reapers.
4.19: And he sayde to his father, Mine head, mine head. Who sayd to his servant, Bear him to his mother.
4.20: And hee took him and brought him to his mother, and hee sat on her knees till noon, and dyed.
4.21: Then she went up, and layed him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door upon him, and went out.
4.22: Then she called to her husband, and sayd, Send with me, I pray thee, one of the yong men and one of the asses: for I will haste to the man of God, and come again.
4.23: And he sayd, Wherefore wilt thou goe to him to day? it is neither new moon nor Sabbath day. And she answered, All shalbe well.
4.24: Then she sadled an ass, and sayde to her servant, Drive, and goe forward: stay not for me to get up, except I bid thee.
4.25: So she went, and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And when the man of God saw her over against him, he sayd to Gehazi his servant, Behold, the Shunammite.
4.26: Runne now, I say, to meet her, and say unto her, Art thou in health? is thine husband in health? and is the child in health? And she answered, We are in health.
4.27: And when she came to the man of God unto the moutaine, she caught him by his feet: and Gehazi went to her, to thrust her away: but the man of God said, Let her alone: for her soul is vexed within her, and the Lord hath hid it from me, and hath not told it mee.
4.28: Then she said, Did I desire a sonne of my lord? did I not say, Deceive me not?
4.29: Then he sayd to Gehazi, Gird thy loynes, and take my staff in thine hand, and goe thy way: if thou meet any, salute him not: and if any salute thee, answer him not: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.
4.30: And the mother of the child sayde, As the Lord liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. Therefore he arose, and followed her.
4.31: But Gehazi was gone before them, and had layed the staff upon the face of the child, but he neither spake nor heard: wherefore hee returned to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not waken.
4.32: Then came Elisha into the house, and behold, the child was dead, and layed upon his bedde.
4.33: He went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twayne, and prayed unto the Lord.
4.34: After he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes upon his eies, and his hands upon his handes, and stretched himself upon him, and the flesh of the child waxed warm.
4.35: And hee went from him, and walked up and down in the house, and went up and spred himself upon him: then the child neesed seven times, and opened his eyes.
4.36: Then he called Gehazi, and sayd, Call this Shunammite. So he called her, which came in unto him. And he said unto her, Take thy sonne.
4.37: And she came, and fell at his feet, and bowed her self to the ground, and took up her sonne, and went out.
4.38: Afterward Elisha returned to Gilgal, and a famine was in the land, and the children of the Prophets dwelt with him. And hee sayd unto his servant, Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage for the children of the Prophets.
4.39: And one went out into the field, to gather herbes, and found, as it were, a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourdes his garment ful, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew it not.
4.40: So they powred out for the men to eat: and when they did eat of the pottage, they cryed out, and sayde, O thou man of God, death is in the pot: and they could not eat thereof.
4.41: Then he said, Bring meal. And hee cast it into the potte, and sayd, Powre out for the people, that they may eat: and there was none evil in the pot.
4.42: Then came a man from Baal-shalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the first fruits, even twenty loaves of barley, and full eares of corn in the husk. And hee said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.
4.43: And his servant answered, How should I set this before an hundreth men? He sayd again, Give it unto the people, that they may eat: for thus sayth the Lord, They shall eat, and there shall remain.
4.44: So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left over, according to the word of the Lord.

5.1: Now was there one Naaman captain of the host of the King of Aram, a great man, and honourable in the sight of his lord, because that by him the Lord had delivered the Aramites. He also was a mightie man and valiant, but a leper.
5.2: And the Aramites had gone out by bands, and had taken a litle mayde of the land of Israel, and she served Naamans wife.
5.3: And she sayd unto her mistres, Would God my lord were with the Prophet that is in Samaria, he would soon deliver him of his leprosie.
5.4: And he went in, and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus saith the mayde that is of the land of Israel.
5.5: And the King of Aram sayde, Goe thy way thither, and I will send a letter unto the King of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten change of rayments,
5.6: And brought the letter to the King of Israel to this effect, Now when this letter is come unto thee, understand, that I have sent thee Naaman my servant, that thou maiest heal him of his leprosie.
5.7: And when the King of Israel had read the letter, he rent his clothes, and sayde, Am I God, to kill and to give life, that hee doth send to mee, that I should heal a man from his leprosie? wherfore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarel against me.
5.8: But when Elisha the man of God had heard that the King of Israel had rent his clothes, hee sent unto the King, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? Let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a Prophet in Israel.
5.9: Then Naaman came with his horses, and with his charets, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
5.10: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash thee in Iorden seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clensed.
5.11: But Naaman was wroth and went away, and sayde, Behold, I thought with my self, Hee will surely come out, and stand, and call on the Name of the Lord his God and put his hand on the place, and heal the leprosie.
5.12: Are not Abanah and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better then all the waters of Israel? may I not wash mee in them, and bee cleansed? so hee turned, and departed in displeasure.
5.13: But his servants came, and spake unto him, and sayd, Father, if the Prophet had commanded thee a great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when hee sayth to thee, Wash and be clean?
5.14: Then went he down, and washed him self seven times in Iorden, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again, like unto ye flesh of a litle child, and he was clean.
5.15: And hee turned again to the man of God, hee, and all his companie, and came and stood before him, and sayd, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the world, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a reward of thy servant.
5.16: But hee sayde, As the Lord liveth (before whom I stand) I wil not receive it. And he would have constrained him to receive it, but he refused.
5.17: Moreover Naaman sayde, Shall there not be given to thy servant two mules loade of this earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt sacrifice nor offring unto any other god, save unto the Lord.
5.18: Herein the Lord bee merciful unto thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon, to worship there, and leaneth on mine hand, and I bow my self in the house of Rimmon: when I doe bow down, I say, in the house of Rimmon, the Lord be merciful unto thy servant in this point.
5.19: Unto whom he said, Goe in peace. So he departed from him about half a dayes journey of ground.
5.20: And Gehazi the servant of Elisha the man of God sayde, Behold, my master hath spared this Aramite Naaman, receiving not those things at his hand that he brought: as the Lord liveth, I will runne after him, and take somewhat of him.
5.21: So Gehazi followed speedily after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he light down from the charet to meet him, and said, Is all well?
5.22: And he answered, All is well: my master hath set me, saying, Behold, there be come to me, even now from mount Ephraim two yong men of the children of the Prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two change of garmets.
5.23: And Naaman said, Yea, take two talents: and he compelled him, and bound two talents of silver in two bagges, with two change of garments, and gave them unto two of his servants, that they might bear them before him.
5.24: And when he came to the towre, he took them out of their handes, and laid them in the house, and sent away the men: and they departed.
5.25: Then he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.
5.26: But he said unto him, Went not mine heart with thee when the man turned again from his charet to meet thee? Is this a time to take money, and to receive garments, and olives, and vineyardes, and sheep, and oxen, and men servants, and maid servants?
5.27: The leprosie therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and to thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper white as snow.

6.1: And the children of the Prophets said unto Elisha, Behold, we pray thee, the place where we dwell with thee, is too litle for us.
6.2: Let us now goe to Iorden, that we may take thence every man a beam, and make us a place to dwell in. And he answered, Goe.
6.3: And one said, Vouchsafe, I pray thee, to go with thy servants, and he answered, I will goe.
6.4: So he went with them, and when they came to Iorden, they cut down wood.
6.5: And as one was felling of a tree, the yron fell into the water: then he cryed, and said, Alas master, it was but borowed.
6.6: And the man of God said, Where fell it? And he shewed him the place. Then he cut down a piece of wood, and cast in thither, and he caused the yron to swimme.
6.7: Then he said, Take it up to thee. And he stretched out his hand, and took it.
6.8: Then the King of Aram warred against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, and said, In such and such a place shalbe my camp.
6.9: Therefore the man of God sent unto the King of Israel, saying, Beware thou goe not over to such a place: for there the Aramites are come down.
6.10: So the King of Israel sent to the place which the man of God told him, and warned him of, and saved himself from thence, not once, nor twise.
6.11: And the heart of the King of Aram was troubled for this thing: therefore he called his servants and said unto them, Will ye not shew me, which of us bewrayeth our counsel to the king of Israel?
6.12: Then one of his servants said, None, my lord, O King, but Elisha the Prophet that is in Israel, telleth the King of Israel, even the wordes that thou speakest in thy priuie chamber.
6.13: And he said, Goe, and espie where he is, that I may send and fetch him. And one told him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothan.
6.14: So he sent thither horses, and charets, and a mightie host: and they came by night, and compassed the citie.
6.15: And when the servant of the man of God arose earely to goe out, behold, an host compassed the citie with horses and charets. Then his servant sayde unto him, Alas master, how shall we doe?
6.16: And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us, are moe then they that be with them.
6.17: Then Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I beseech thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the servant, and he looked, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and charets of fyre round about Elisha.
6.18: So they came down to him, but Elisha prayed unto the Lord, and said, Smite this people, I pray thee, with blindness. And he smote them with blindnes, according to the word of Elisha.
6.19: And Elisha said unto them, This is not the way, neither is this the citie: follow me, and I will lead you to the man whom ye seek. But he ledde them to Samaria.
6.20: And when they were come to Samaria, Elisha said, Lord, open their eyes that they may see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw, and behold, they were in the mids of Samaria.
6.21: And the King of Israel sayde unto Elisha when he saw them, My father, shall I smite them, shall I smite them?
6.22: And he answered, Thou shalt not smite them: doest thou not smite them that thou hast taken with thy sword, and with thy bow? but set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink and goe to their master.
6.23: And he made great preparation for them: and when they had eaten and drunken, he sent them away: and they went to their master. So ye bands of Aram came no more into the land of Israel.
6.24: But afterward Ben-hadad King of Aram gathered all his host, and went up, and besieged Samaria.
6.25: So there was a great famine in Samaria: for loe, they besieged it until an asses head was at four score pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a kab of doves doung at five pieces of silver.
6.26: And as the King of Israel was going upon the wall, there cryed a woman unto him, saying, Help, my lord, O King.
6.27: And he said, Seeing the Lord doeth not succour thee, how should I help thee with the barn, or with the wine press?
6.28: Also the King said unto her, What ayleth thee? And she answered, This woman sayde unto me, Give thy sonne, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my sonne to morowe,
6.29: So we sod my sonne, and did eat him: and I said to her the day after, Give thy sonne, that we may eat him, but she hath hid her sonne.
6.30: And when the King had heard the wordes of the woman, he rent his clothes, (and as he went upon the wall, the people looked, and behold, he had sackecloth within upon his flesh)
6.31: And he said, God doe so to me and more also, if the head of Elisha the sonne of Shaphat shall stand on him this day.
6.32: (Now Elisha sat in his house, and the Elders sat with him.) And the King sent a man before him: but before the messenger came to him, he said to the Elders, See ye not how this murtherers sonne hath sent to take away mine head? take heed when the messenger cometh, and shut the door and handle him roughly at the door: is not the sound of his masters feet behind him?
6.33: While he yet talked with them, behold, the messenger came down unto him, and said, Behold, this evil cometh of the Lord: should I attend on the Lord any longer?

7.1: Then Elisha said, Hear ye the word of the Lord: thus saith the Lord, To morowe this time a measure of fine flour shalbe sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel in the gate of Samaria.
7.2: Then a prince, on whose hand the King leaned, answered the man of God, and said, Though the Lord would make windowes in the heaven, could this thing come to pass? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not eat thereof.
7.3: Now there were four leprous men at the entring in of the gate: and they said one to an other, Why sitte we here until we die?
7.4: If we say, We will enter into the citie, the famine is in the citie, and we shall die there: and if we sit here, we dye also. Now therefore come, and let us fall into the camp of the Aramites: if they save our lives, we shall live: and if they kill us, we are but dead.
7.5: So they rose up in the twilight, to goe to the camp of the Aramites: and when they were come to the utmost part of the camp of the Aramites, loe, there was no man there.
7.6: For the Lord had caused the camp of the Aramites to hear a noyse of charets and a noise of horses, and a noise of a great armie, so that they sayde one to another, Behold, the King of Israel hath hired against us the Kings of the Hittites, and the Kings of the Egyptians to come upon us.
7.7: Wherefore they arose, and fled in the twilight, and left their tentes and their horses, and their asses, even the camp as it was, and fledde for their lives.
7.8: And when these lepers came to the utmost part of the camp, they entred into one tent, and did eat and drink, and caryed thence silver and gold, and raiment, and went and hid it: after they returned, and entred into another tent, and caryed thence also, and went and hid it.
7.9: Then said one to another, We doe not well: this day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace. if we tary till day light, some mischief will come upon us. Now therefore, come, let us goe, and tell the Kings housholde.
7.10: So they came, and called unto the porters of the citie, and told them, saying, We came to the camp of the Aramites, and loe, there was no man there, neither voyce of man, but horses tyed and asses tyed: and the tents are as they were.
7.11: And the porters cryed and declared to the Kings house within.
7.12: Then the King arose in the night, and said unto his servants, I wil shew you now, what the Aramites have done unto us. They know that we are affamished, therefore they are gone out of the camp to hide them selves in the field, saying, When they come out of the citie, we shall catch them alive, and get into the citie.
7.13: And one of his servants answered, and said, Let me take now five of the horses that remain, and are left in the citie, (behold, they are even as all the multitude of Israel that are left therein: behold, I say, they are as the multitude of the Israelites that are consumed) and we wil send to see.
7.14: So they took two charets of horses, and the King sent after the host of the Aramites, saying, Goe and see.
7.15: And they went after them unto Iorden, and loe, all the way was full of clothes and vessels which the Aramites had cast from them in their hast: and the messengers returned, and told ye King.
7.16: Then the people went out and spoyled the camp of the Aramites: so a measure of fine flour was at a shekel, and two measures of barley at a shekel according to the word of the Lord.
7.17: And the King gave the prince (on whose hand he leaned) the charge of the gate, and the people trode upon him in the gate, and he dyed, as the man of God had said, which spake it, when the King came down to him.
7.18: And it came to pass, as the man of God had spoken to the King, saying, Two measures of barley at a shekel, and a measure of fine flour shall be at a shekel, to morowe about this time in the gate of Samaria.
7.19: But the prince had answered the man of God, and said, Though the Lord would make windowes in the heaven, could it come so to pass? And he said, Behold, thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not eat thereof.
7.20: And so it came unto him: for the people trode upon him in the gate, and he dyed.

8.1: Then spake Elisha unto the woman, whose sonne he had restored to life, saying, Up, and goe, thou, and thine house, and soiourne where thou canst soiourne: for the Lord hath called for a famine, and it cometh also upon the land seven yeeres.
8.2: And the woman arose, and did after the saying of the man of God, and went both she and her housholde and soiourned in the land of the Philistims seven yeeres.
8.3: And at the seven yeeres end, the woman returned out of the land of the Philistims, and went out to call upon the King for her house and for her land.
8.4: And the King talked with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell mee, I pray thee, all the great actes, that Elisha hath done.
8.5: And as he told the King, how he had restored one dead to life, behold, the woman, whose sonne he had raised to life, called upon the King for her house and for her land. Then Gehazi sayd, My lord, O King, this is the woman, and this is her sonne, whom Elisha restored to life.
8.6: And when the King asked the woman, she told him: so the King appoynted her an Eunuch, saying, Restore thou all that are hers, and all the fruites of her landes since the day she left the land, even until this time.
8.7: Then Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad the King of Aram was sick, and one told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
8.8: And the king sayd unto Hazael, Take a present in thine hand, and goe meet the man of God, that thou mayest inquire of ye Lord by him, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
8.9: So Hazael went to meet him, and took the present in his hand, and of every good thing of Damascus, even the burden of fourtie camels, and came and stood before him, and sayde, Thy sonne Ben-hadad King of Aram hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this disease?
8.10: And Elisha sayd to him, Goe, and say unto him, Thou shalt recover: howbeit the Lord hath shewed me, that he shall surely dye.
8.11: And hee looked upon him stedfastly, till Hazael was ashamed, and the man of God wept.
8.12: And Hazael sayde, Why weepeth my lord? And he answered, Because I know the evil that thou shalt do unto the children of Israel: for their strong cities shalt thou set on fire, and their yong men shalt thou slay with the sword, and shalt dash their infantes against the stones, and rent in pieces their women with child.
8.13: Then Hazael said, What? is thy servant a dog, that I should doe this great thing? And Elisha answered, The Lord hath shewed mee, that thou shalt be King of Aram.
8.14: So he departed from Elisha, and came to his master, who said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he answered, Hee told mee that thou shouldest recover.
8.15: And on the morow he took a thick cloth and dipt in it water, and spread it on his face, and hee dyed: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
8.16: Now in the fift yere of Joram ye sonne of Ahab King of Israel, and of Jehoshaphat King of Judah, Jehoram the sonne of Jehoshaphat King of Judah began to reign.
8.17: He was two and thirtie yere old, when he began to reign: and hee reigned eight yeere in Jerusalem.
8.18: And hee walked in the wayes of the Kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife, and hee did evil in the sight of the Lord.
8.19: Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah, for David his servants sake, as he had promised him to give him a light, and to his children for ever.
8.20: In those dayes Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and made a King over themselves.
8.21: Therefore Joram went to Zair, and all his charets with him, and he arose by night, and smote the Edomites which were about him with the captains of the charets, and the people fled into their tents.
8.22: So Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah unto this day. then Libnah rebelled at that same time.
8.23: Concerning the rest of the actes of Joram and all that hee did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
8.24: And Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the citie of David. And Ahaziah his sonne reigned in his stead.
8.25: In the twelft yere of Joram the sonne of Ahab King of Israel did Ahaziah the sonne of Jehoram King of Judah begin to reign.
8.26: Two and twentie yeere old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one yere in Jerusalem, and his mothers name was Athaliah the daughter of Omri King of Israel.
8.27: And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, like the house of Ahab: for hee was the sonne in law of the house of Ahab.
8.28: And he went with Joram the sonne of Ahab to war against Hazael King of Aram in Ramoth Gilead, and the Aramites smote Joram.
8.29: And King Joram returned to bee healed in Izreel of the wounds which ye Aramites had given him at Ramah, whe he fought against Hazael King of Aram. And Ahaziah the sonne of Jehoram King of Judah went down to see Joram the sonne of Ahab in Izreel, because he was sick.

9.1: Then Elisha the Prophet called one of ye children of the Prophets, and sayde unto him, Gird thy loynes and take this box of oyle in thine hand and get thee to Ramoth Gilead.
9.2: And when thou comest thither, look where is Jehu ye sonne of Jehoshaphat, the sonne of Nimshi, and go, and make him arise up from among his brethren, and lead him to a secret chamber.
9.3: Then take the box of oyle and powre it on his head, and say, Thus sayth the Lord, I have anointed thee for King over Israel. then open the door, and flee without any tarying.
9.4: So the seruat of ye Prophet gate him to Ramoth Gilead.
9.5: And when he came in, behold, the captaines of the armie were sitting. And he sayde, I have a message to thee, O captain. And Jehu sayd, Unto which of all us? And he answered, To thee, O captain.
9.6: And he arose, and went into the house, and he powred the oyle on his head and sayde unto him, Thus sayth the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed thee for King over the people of the Lord, even over Israel.
9.7: And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the Prophets, and the blood of al the servants of the Lord of the hand of Jezebel.
9.8: For the whole house of Ahab shalbe destroied: and I will cut off from Ahab, him that maketh water against the wall, as well him that is shut up, as him that is left in Israel.
9.9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the sonne of Ahiiah.
9.10: And the dogges shall eat Jezebel in the field of Izreel, and there shalbe none to burie her. And he opened the door, and fled.
9.11: Then Jehu came out to the servants of his lord. And one sayd unto him, Is all well? wherefore came this mad fellow to thee? And hee sayde unto them, Ye know the man, and what his talk was.
9.12: And they sayde, It is false, tell us it now. Then he sayd, Thus and thus spake he to me, saying, Thus saieth the Lord, I have anointed thee for King over Israel.
9.13: Then they made haste, and took euerie man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the staires, and blew the trumpet, saying, Jehu is King.
9.14: So Jehu ye sonne of Jehoshaphat the sonne of Nimshi conspired against Joram: (Now Joram kept Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael King of Aram.
9.15: And King Joram returned to bee healed in Izreel of the woundes, which the Aramites had given him, when hee fought with Hazael King of Aram) and Jehu sayde, If it be your mindes, let no man depart and escape out of the citie, to goe and tell in Izreel.
9.16: So Jehu gate up into a charet, and went to Izreel: for Joram lay there, and Ahaziah King of Judah was come down to see Joram.
9.17: And the watchman that stood in the towre in Izreel spyed the companie of Jehu as hee came, and sayd, I see a companie. And Jehoram said, Take a horseman and send to meet them, that hee may say, Is it peace?
9.18: So there went one on horseback to meet him, and sayde, Thus sayth the King, Is it peace? And Jehu sayd, What hast thou to do with peace? Turn behind me. And the watchman told, saying, The messenger came to them, but he cometh not again.
9.19: Then hee sent out another on horseback, which came to them, and sayde, Thus sayth the King, Is it peace? And Jehu answered, What hast thou to doe with peace? turn behind me.
9.20: And the watchman told, saying, He came to them also, but cometh not again, and the marching is like the marching of Jehu the sonne of Nimshi: for he marcheth furiously.
9.21: Then Jehoram sayd, Make ready: and his charet was made ready. And Jehoram King of Israel and Ahaziah King of Judah went out eyther of them in his charet against Jehu, and met him in the field of Naboth the Izreelite.
9.22: And when Jehoram saw Jehu, he sayde, Is it peace, Jehu? And he answered, What peace? whiles the whoredomes of thy mother Jezebel, and her witchcraftes are yet in great nomber?
9.23: Then Jehoram turned his hand, and fled, and said to Ahaziah, O Ahaziah, there is treason.
9.24: But Jehu took a bow in his hand, and smote Jehoram between the shoulders, that the arowe went through his heart: and he fell down in his charet.
9.25: Then said Jehu to Bidkar a captain, Take, and cast him in some place of the field of Naboth the Izreelite: for I remember that when I and thou rode together after Ahab his father, the Lord layed this burden upon him.
9.26: Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sonnes, said the Lord, and I will render it thee in this field, saith the Lord: now therefore take and cast him in the field, according to the word of the Lord.
9.27: But when Ahaziah the King of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of the garden house: And Jehu pursued after him, and sayd, Smite him also in the charet: and they smote him in the going up to Gur, which is by Ibleam. And hee fled to Megiddo, and there dyed.
9.28: And his servants caried him in a charet to Jerusalem, and buried him in his sepulchre with his fathers in the citie of David.
9.29: And in the eleventh yere of Joram the sonne of Ahab, began Ahaziah to reign over Judah.
9.30: And when Jehu was come to Izreel, Jezebel heard of it, and painted her face, and tired her head, and looked out at a window.
9.31: And as Jehu entred at the gate, she sayde, Had Zimri peace, which slew his master?
9.32: And he lift up his eyes to the window, and sayd, Who is on my side, who? Then two or three of her Eunuches looked unto him.
9.33: And he sayde, Cast her down: and they cast her down, and hee sprinkled of her blood upon the wall, and upon the horses, and he trode her under foot.
9.34: And when he was come in, he did eat and drink, and sayde, Visit now yonder cursed woman, and burie her: for she is a Kings daughter.
9.35: And they went to burie her, but they foud no more of her, then the skull and the feet, and the palmes of her handes.
9.36: Wherefore they came agayne and told him. And he said, This is the word of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Eliiah the Tishbite, saying, In the field of Izreel shall ye dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel.
9.37: And the carkeis of Jezebel shalbe as doung upon the ground in the field of Izreel, so that none shall say, This is Jezebel.

10.1: Ahab had now seuentie sonnes in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters, and sent to Samaria unto the rulers of Izreel, and to the Elders, and to the bringers up of Ahabs children, to this effect,
10.2: Now when this letter cometh to you, (for ye have with you your masters sonnes, yee have with you both charets and horses, and a defenced citie, and armour)
10.3: Consider therefore which of your masters sonnes is best and most meet, and set him on his fathers throne, and fight for your masters house.
10.4: But they were exceedingly afraid, and said, Behold two Kings could not stand before him, how shall we then stand?
10.5: And he that was gouernour of Ahabs house, and he that ruled the citie, and the Elders, and the bringers up of the children sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and will doe all that thou shalt bid us: we will make no King: do what seemeth good to thee.
10.6: Then he wrote another letter to them, saying, If ye be mine, and wil obey my voyce, take the heads of ye men that are your masters sonnes, and come to me to Izreel by to morowe this time. (Now the Kings sonnes, even seuentie persons were with the great men of the citie, which brought them up)
10.7: And when the letter came to them, they took the Kings sonnes, and slew the seuentie persons, and layde their heads in baskets, and sent them unto him to Izreel.
10.8: Then there came a messenger and told him, saying, They have brought the heads of the Kings sonnes. And he sayd, Let them lay them on two heapes at the entring in of the gate until the morning.
10.9: And when it was day, he went out, and stood and sayd to all the people, Ye be righteous: behold, I conspired against my master, and slew him: but who slew all these?
10.10: Know now that there shall fall unto the earth nothing of the word of the Lord, which the Lord spake concerning the house of Ahab: for the Lord hath brought to pass the things that hee spake by his servant Eliiah.
10.11: So Jehu slew al that remained of the house of Ahab in Izreel, and all that were great with him, and his familiars and his priestes, so that he let none of his remain.
10.12: And he arose, and departed and came to Samaria. And as Jehu was in the way by an house where the shepheards did shere,
10.13: He met with the brethre of Ahaziah king of Judah, and sayd, Who are ye? And they answered, We are the brethren of Ahaziah, and goe down to salute the children of the King and the children of the Queen.
10.14: And he sayde, Take them alive. And they took them alive, and slew them at the well beside the house where the sheep are shorn, even two and fourtie men, and he left not one of them.
10.15: And when he was departed thence, hee met with Jehonadab the sonne of Rechab coming to meet him, and he blessed him, and sayde to him, Is thine heart upright, as mine heart is toward thine? And Jehonadab answered, Yea, doubtless. Then give me thine hand. And when he had given him his hand, he took him up to him into the charet.
10.16: And he sayde, Come with me, and see the zeal that I have for the Lord: so they made him ride in his charet.
10.17: And when he came to Samaria, he slew all that remained unto Ahab in Samaria, till he had destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake to Eliiah.
10.18: Then Jehu assembled all the people, and sayd unto them, Ahab served Baal a litle, but Jehu shall serve him much more.
10.19: Now therefore call unto me all ye prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests, and let not a man be lacking: for I have a great sacrifice for Baal: whosoever is lacking, he shall not live. But Jehu did it by a subtiltie to destroy ye seruats of Baal.
10.20: And Jehu sayd, Proclaim a solemn assemblie for Baal. And they proclaimed it.
10.21: So Jehu sent unto all Israel, and all the servants of Baal came, and there was not a man left that came not. And they came into the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was full from end to end.
10.22: Then he said unto him that had the charge of the vestrie, Bring forth vestments for al the servants of Baal. And he brought the out vestments.
10.23: And when Jehu went, and Jehonadab the sonne of Rechab into the house of Baal, he sayde unto the servants of Baal, Search diligently, and look, lest there be here with you any of the servants of the Lord, but the servants of Baal only.
10.24: And when they went in to make sacrifice and burnt offering, Jehu appoynted four score men without, and sayd, If any of the men whom I have brought into your hands, escape, his soul shalbe for his soul.
10.25: And when hee had made an end of the burnt offring, Jehu sayde to the garde, and to the captaines, Goe in, slay them, let not a man come out. And they smote them with the edge of the sword. And the garde, and the captaines cast them out, and went unto the citie, where was the temple of Baal.
10.26: And they brought out the images of the temple of Baal, and burnt them.
10.27: And they destroyed the image of Baal, and threw down the house of Baal, and made a iakes of it unto this day.
10.28: So Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
10.29: But from the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat which made Israel to sinne, Jehu departed not from them, neither from the golden calves that were in Beth-el and that were in Dan.
10.30: And the Lord sayde unto Jehu, Because thou hast diligently executed that which was right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all things that were in mine heart, therefore shall thy sonnes unto the fourth generation sit on the throne of Israel.
10.31: But Jehu regarded not to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart: for hee departed not from the sinnes of Jeroboam, which made Israel to sinne.
10.32: In those dayes the Lord began to lothe Israel, and Hazael smote them in all the coastes of Israel,
10.33: From Iorden Eastward, even all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and them that were of Manasseh, from Aroer (which is by the river Arnon) and Gilead and Bashan.
10.34: Concerning the rest of the actes of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his valiant deedes, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
10.35: And Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buryed him in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his sonne reigned in his stead.
10.36: And the time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria is eight and twentie yeeres.

11.1: Then Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah when she saw that her sonne was dead, she arose, and destroyed all the Kings seed.
11.2: But Jehosheba the daughter of King Joram, and sister to Ahaziah took Joash the sonne of Ahaziah, and stale him from among the Kings sonnes that should be slain, both him and his nource, keeping them in the bed chaber, and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
11.3: And he was with her hid in the house of the Lord six yeere: and Athaliah did reign over the land.
11.4: And the seventh yeere Jehoiada sent and took the captaines over hundreths, with other captaines and them of the garde, and caused them to come unto him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant with them, and took an othe of them in the house of the Lord, and shewed them the Kings sonne.
11.5: And he commanded them, saying, This is it that ye must doe, The third part of you, that cometh on the Sabbath, shall ward toward the Kings house:
11.6: And another third part in the gate of Sur: and another third part in the gate behind them of the garde: and ye shall keep watch in the house of Massah.
11.7: And two parts of you, that is, all that goe out on the Sabbath day, shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the King.
11.8: And ye shall compass the King round about, every man with his weapon in his hand, and whosoever cometh within the ranges, let him be slayne: be you with the King, as he goeth out and in.
11.9: And the captaines of the hundreths did according to all that Jehoiada the Priest commaded, and they took every man his men that entred in to their charge on the Sabbath with them that went out of it on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the Priest.
11.10: And the Priest gave to the captaines of hundreths the speares and the shieldes that were King Dauids, and were in the house of the Lord.
11.11: And the garde stood, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side, about the altar and about the house, round about the King.
11.12: Then he brought out the Kings sonne, and put the crown upon him and gave him the Testimonie, and they made him King: also they anoynted him, and clapt their handes, and sayde, God save the King.
11.13: And when Athaliah heard the noyse of the running of the people, she came in to the people in the house of the Lord.
11.14: And when she looked, behold, the King stood by a pillar, as the maner was, and the princes and the trumpeters by the King, and al the people of the land reioyced, and blew with trumpets. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and cryed, Treason, treason.
11.15: But Jehoiada the Priest commanded the captaines of the hundreths that had the rule of the host, and sayde unto them, Have her forth of the ranges, and he that followeth her, let him die by the sword: for the Priest had sayd, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.
11.16: Then they laid hands on her, and she went by the way, by the which the horses goe to the house of the King, and there was she slain.
11.17: And Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, and the King and the people, that they should be the Lordes people: likewise between the King and the people.
11.18: Then all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and destroyed it with his altars, and his images brake they down courageously, and slew Mattan the Priest of Baal before the altars: and the Priest set a garde over the house of the Lord.
11.19: Then he took the captaines of hudreths, and the other captaines, and the garde, and all the people of the land: and they brought the King from the house of the Lord, and came by the way of the gate of the garde to the Kings house: and he sat him down on the throne of the Kings.
11.20: And all the people of the land reioyced, and the citie was in quiet: for they had slain Athaliah with the sword beside the Kings house.
11.21: Seven yeere old was Jehoash when he began to reign.

12.1: In the seventh yere of Jehu Jehoash began to reign, and reigned fourty yeres in Jerusalem, and his mothers name was Zibiah of Beer-sheba.
12.2: And Jehoash did that which was good in the sight of the Lord all his time that Jehoiada the Priest taught him.
12.3: But the hie places were not taken away: for the people offred yet and burnt incense in the hie places.
12.4: And Jehoash sayde to the Priestes, All the silver of dedicate things that bee brought to the house of the Lord, that is, the money of them that are under the count, the money that every man is set at, and all the money that one offereth willingly, and bringeth into the house of the Lord,
12.5: Let the Priestes take it to them, every man of his acquaintance: and they shall repair the broken places of the house, wheresoever any decay is found.
12.6: Yet in the three and twentieth yeere of King Jehoash the Priestes had not mended that which was decayed in the Temple.
12.7: Then King Jehoash called for Jehoiada the Priest, and the other Priestes, and sayd unto them, Why repair yee not the ruines of the Temple? now therefore receive no more money of your acquaintance, except yee deliver it to repair the ruines of the Temple.
12.8: So the Priestes consented to receive no more money of the people, neither to repair the decayed places of the Temple.
12.9: Then Jehoiada the Priest took a chest and bored an hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side, as every man cometh into the Temple of the Lord. And the Priestes that kept the door, put therein all the money that was brought into the house of the Lord.
12.10: And when they saw there was much money in the chest, the Kinges Secretarie came up and the hie Priest, and put it up after that they had told the money that was found in the house of the Lord,
12.11: And they gave the money made readie into the handes of them, that vndertooke the work, and that had the oversight of the house of the Lord; and they payed it out to the carpenters and builders that wrought upon the house of the Lord,
12.12: And to the masons and hewers of stone, and to bye timber and hewed stone, to repayre that was decayed in the house of the Lord, and for all that which was layed out for the reparation of the Temple.
12.13: Howbeit there was not made for the house of the Lord bowles of silver, instruments of musick, basons, trumpets, nor any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver of the money that was brought into the house of the Lord.
12.14: But they gave it to the workemen, which repayred therewith the house of the Lord.
12.15: Moreover, they reckoned not with the men, into whose handes they delivered that money to be bestowed on workemen: for they dealt faithfully.
12.16: The money of the trespass offring and the money of ye sinne offrings was not brought into the house of the Lord: for it was the Priests.
12.17: Then came up Hazael King of Aram, and fought against Gath and took it, and Hazael set his face to goe up to Jerusalem.
12.18: And Jehoash King of Judah took all the halowed thinges that Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram, and Ahaziah his fathers Kings of Judah had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord and in the Kings house, and sent it to Hazael King of Aram, and he departed from Jerusalem.
12.19: Concerning the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
12.20: And his servants arose and wrought treason, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, when he came down to Silla:
12.21: Even Jozachar the sonne of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the sonne of Shomer his servants smote him, and he dyed: and they buried him with his fathers in the citie of David. And Amaziah his sonne reigned in his stead.

13.1: In the three and twentieth yeere of Joash the sonne of Ahaziah King of Judah, Jehoahaz the sonne of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen yeere.
13.2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and followed the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne, and departed not therefrom.
13.3: And the Lord was angry with Israel, and delivered them into the hand of Hazael King of Aram, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the sonne of Hazael, all his dayes.
13.4: And Jehoahaz besought the Lord, and the Lord heard him: for he saw the trouble of Israel, wherewith the King of Aram troubled them.
13.5: (And the Lord gave Israel a deliverer, so that they came out from under the subiection of the Aramites. And the children of Israel dwelt in their tents as before time.
13.6: Nevertheless they departed not from the sinnes of the house of Jeroboam which made Israel sinne, but walked in them. even the grove also remayned still in Samaria)
13.7: For he had left of the people to Jehoahaz but fiftie horsemen, and tenne charets, and tenne thousand footemen, because the King of Aram had destroyed them, and made them like dust beaten to pouder.
13.8: Concerning the rest of the actes of Jehoahaz and all that he did, and his valiant deedes, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
13.9: And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Joash his sonne reigned in his stead.
13.10: In the seven and thirtieth yere of Joash King of Judah began Jehoash the sonne of Jehoahaz to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned sixteen yeere,
13.11: And did evil in the sight of the Lord: for he departed not from all the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat that made Israel to sinne, but he walked therein.
13.12: Concerning the rest of the actes of Joash and all that he did, and his valiant deedes, and how he fought against Amaziah King of Judah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
13.13: And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his seat: and Joash was buryed in Samaria among the Kings of Israel.
13.14: When Elisha fell sick of his sickenesse whereof he dyed, Joash the King of Israel came down unto him, and wept upon his face, and sayd, O my father, my father, the charet of Israel, and the horsemen of the same.
13.15: Then Elisha sayde unto him, Take a bow and arrowes. And he took unto him bow and arrowes.
13.16: And he sayde to the King of Israel, Put thine hand upon the bow. And he put his hand upon it. And Elisha put his hands upon the Kings hands,
13.17: And said, Open the window Eastward. And when he had opened it, Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he sayd, Behold the arrow of the Lordes deliverance and the arrow of deliverance against Aram: for thou shalt smite the Aramites in Aphek, till thou hast consumed them.
13.18: Again he said, Take the arrowes. And he took them. And he sayde unto the King of Israel, Smite the ground. And he smote thrise, and ceased.
13.19: Then the man of God was angry with him, and sayde, Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times, so thou shouldest have smitten Aram, till thou haddest consumed it, where now thou shalt smite Aram but thrise.
13.20: So Elisha dyed, and they buryed him. And certain bandes of the Moabites came into the land that yeere.
13.21: And as they were burying a man, behold, they saw the souldiers: therfore they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha. And when the man was down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood upon his feet.
13.22: But Hazael King of Aram vexed Israel all the dayes of Jehoahaz.
13.23: Therefore the Lord had mercy on them and pitied them, and had respect unto them because of his covenant with Abraham, Izhak, and Iaakob, and would not destroy them, neither cast he them from him as yet.
13.24: So Hazael the King of Aram dyed: and Ben-hadad his sonne reigned in his stead.
13.25: Therefore Jehoash the sonne of Jehoahaz returned, and took out of the hand of Ben-hadad the sonne of Hazael the cities which he had taken away by war out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father: for three times did Joash beat him, and restored the cities unto Israel.

14.1: The second yeere of Joash sonne of Jehoahaz King of Israel reigned Amaziah the sonne of Joash King of Judah.
14.2: He was five and twentie yeere old when he began to reign, and reigned nine and twentie yeere in Jerusalem, and his mothers name was Iehoadan of Jerusalem.
14.3: And he did uprightly in the sight of the Lord, yet not like David his father, but did according to all that Joash his father had done.
14.4: Notwithstanding the hie places were not taken away: for as yet the people did sacrifice and burnt incense in the hie places.
14.5: And when the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, he slew his servants which had killed the King his father.
14.6: But the children of those that did slay him, he slew not, according unto that that is written in the book of the Law of Moses, wherein the Lord commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children put to death for the fathers: but every man shall be put to death for his own sinne.
14.7: He slew also of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took the citie of Sela by war, and called the name thereof Joktheel unto this day.
14.8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash the sonne of Jehoahaz, sonne of Jehu King of Israel, saying, Come, let us see one another in the face.
14.9: Then Jehoash the King of Israel sent to Amaziah King of Judah, saying, The thistle that is in Lebanon, sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my sonne to wife: and the wild beast that was in Lebanon, went and trode down the thistle.
14.10: Because thou hast smitten Edom, thine heart hath made thee proud: bragge of glory, and tary at home. why doest thou provoke to thine hurt, that thou shouldest fall, and Judah with thee?
14.11: But Amaziah would not hear: therefore Jehoash King of Israel went up: and he and Amaziah King of Judah saw one another in the face at Beth-shemesh which is in Judah.
14.12: And Judah was put to the worse before Israel, and they fledde every man to their tents.
14.13: But Jehoash King of Israel took Amaziah King of Judah, the sonne of Jehoash the sonne of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and came to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundreth cubites.
14.14: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the Kings house, and the children that were in hostage, and returned to Samaria.
14.15: Concerning the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did and his valiant deedes, and how he fought with Amaziah King of Judah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
14.16: And Jehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried at Samaria among the Kings of Israel: and Jeroboam his sonne reigned in his stead.
14.17: And Amaziah the sonne of Joash King of Judah, lived after the death of Jehoash sonne of Jehoahaz King of Israel fifteen yeere.
14.18: Concerning the rest of the actes of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
14.19: But they wrought treason against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish, but they sent after him to Lachish, and slew him there.
14.20: And they brought him on horses, and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in the citie of David.
14.21: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah which was sixteen yeere old, and made him King for his father Amaziah.
14.22: He built Elath, and restored it to Judah, after that the King slept with his fathers.
14.23: In the fifteenth yeere of Amaziah the sonne of Joash King of Judah, was Jeroboam the sonne of Joash made King over Israel in Samaria, and reigned one and fourtie yeere.
14.24: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord: for he departed not from all the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne.
14.25: He restored the coast of Israel, from the entring of Hamath, unto the Sea of the wilderness, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by his servant Jonah the sonne of Amittai the Prophet, which was of Gath Hepher.
14.26: For the Lord saw the exceeding bitter affliction of Israel, so that there was none shutte up, nor any left, neyther yet any that could help Israel.
14.27: Yet the Lord had not decreed to put out the name of Israel from under the heaven: therefore he preserved them by the hand of Jeroboam the sonne of Joash.
14.28: Concerning the rest of the actes of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his valiant deedes, and how he fought, and how he restored Damascus, and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
14.29: So Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the Kings of Israel, and Zachariah his sonne reigned in his stead.

15.1: In the seven and twentieth yeere of Jeroboam King of Israel, began Azariah, sonne of Amaziah King of Judah to reign.
15.2: Sixteen yeere old was he, when he was made King, and he reigned two and fiftie yeere in Jerusalem: and his mothers name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
15.3: And he did uprightly in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah did.
15.4: But the hie places were not put away: for the people yet offered, and burned incense in the hie places.
15.5: And the Lord smote the King: and he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in an house apart, and Jotham the kings sonne gouerned the house, and judged the people of the land.
15.6: Concerning the rest of the actes of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
15.7: So Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buryed him with his fathers in the citie of David, and Jotham his sonne reigned in his stead.
15.8: In the eyght and thirtieth yeere of Azariah King of Judah did Zachariah the sonne of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six moneths,
15.9: And did evil in the sight of the Lord, as did his fathers: for he departed not from the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne.
15.10: And Shallum the sonne of Jabesh cospired against him, and smote him in the sight of the people, and killed him, and reigned in his stead.
15.11: Concerning the rest of the actes of Zachariah, behold, they are written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
15.12: This was the word of the Lord, which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sonnes shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation after thee. And it came so to pass.
15.13: Shallum the sonne of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth yeere of Uzziah King of Judah: and he reigned the space of a moneth in Samaria.
15.14: For Menahem the sonne of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the sonne of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
15.15: Cocerning the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the treason which he wrought, behold, they are written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
15.16: Then Menahem destroyed Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coastes thereof from Tirzah, because they opened not to him, and he smote it, and ript up all their women with child.
15.17: The nine and thirtieth yeere of Azariah King of Judah, beganne Menahem the sonne of Gadi to reign over Israel, and reigned ten yeeres in Samaria.
15.18: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and departed not all his dayes from the sinne of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne.
15.19: Then Pul the king of Asshur came against the land: and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might bee with him, and establish the kingdom in his hand.
15.20: And Menahem exacted the money in Israel, that all men of substance should give the King of Asshur fiftie shekels of silver a piece: so the king of Asshur returned and taried not there in the land.
15.21: Concerning the rest of the actes of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
15.22: And Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his sonne did reign in his stead.
15.23: In ye fiftieth yere of Azariah king of Judah, began Pekahiah the sonne of Menahem to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two yere.
15.24: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord: for he departed not from the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne.
15.25: And Pekah the sonne of Remaliah, his captain conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria in the place of the Kings palace with Argob and Arieh, and with him fiftie men of the Gileadites: so he killed him, and reigned in his stead.
15.26: Concerning the rest of the actes of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
15.27: In the two and fiftieth yere of Azariah King of Judah began Pekah the sonne of Remaliah to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twentie yeere.
15.28: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord: for he departed not from the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, that made Israel to sinne.
15.29: In the dayes of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath Pileser king of Asshur, and took Iion, and Abel, Beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilah, and all the land of Naphtali, and caryed them away to Asshur.
15.30: And Hoshea the sonne of Elah wrought treason against Pekah the sonne of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead in the twentieth yeere of Jotham the sonne of Uzziah.
15.31: Concerning the rest of the actes of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
15.32: In the second yere of Pekah the sonne of Remaliah King of Israel, began Jotham sonne of Uzziah King of Judah to reign.
15.33: Five and twentie yeere old was he, when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen yeere in Jerusalem: and his mothers name was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
15.34: And hee did uprightly in the sight of the Lord: he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
15.35: But the hie places were not put away: for the people yet offered and burnt incense in the hie places: he buylt the hyest gate of the house of the Lord.
15.36: Concerning the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that hee did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
15.37: In those dayes the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Aram, and Pekah the sonne of Remaliah.
15.38: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buryed with his fathers in the citie of David his father, and Ahaz his sonne reigned in his stead.

16.1: The seventeenth yeere of Pekah the sonne of Remaliah, Ahaz the sonne of Jotham King of Judah began to reign.
16.2: Twentie yeere old was Ahaz, when hee began to reign, and he reigned sixteen yeere in Jerusalem, and did not uprightly in the sight of the Lord his God, like David his father:
16.3: But walked in the way of ye kings of Israel, yea, and made his sonne to go through the fire, after the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.
16.4: Also he offred and burnt incense in the hie places and on the hilles, and under every green tree.
16.5: Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah sonne of Remaliah King of Israel came up to Jerusalem to fight: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.
16.6: At the same time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram, and drove the Iewes from Elath: so the Aramites came to Elath, and dwelt there unto this day.
16.7: Then Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath Pileser king of Asshur, saying, I am thy servant and thy sonne: come up, and deliver me out of the hand of the king of Aram, and out of the hand of the King of Israel which rise up against me.
16.8: And Ahaz took the silver and the gold that was found in the house of the Lord, and in the treasures of the Kings house, and sent a present unto the King of Asshur.
16.9: And the King of Asshur consented unto him: and the King of Asshur went up against Damascus. and when he had taken it, he caryed the people away to Kir, and slew Rezin.
16.10: And King Ahaz went unto Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser King of Asshur: and when King Ahaz saw the altar that was at Damascus, he sent to Vriiah the Priest the paterne of the altar, and the facion of it, and all the workemanship thereof.
16.11: And Vriiah the Priest made an altar in al poyntes like to that which King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so did Vriiah the Priest against King Ahaz came from Damascus.
16.12: So when the King was come from Damascus, the King saw the altar: and the King drew neere to the altar and offered thereon.
16.13: And hee burnt his burnt offering, and his meat offring, and powred his drink offring, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offrings besides the altar,
16.14: And set it by the brasen altar which was before the Lord, and brought it in farther before the house between the altar and the house of the Lord, and set it on the North side of the altar.
16.15: And King Ahaz commanded Vriiah the Priest, and sayde, Upon the great altar set on fire in the morning the burnt offring, and in the even the meat offring, and the Kings burnt offring and his meat offering, with the burnt offring of all the people of the land, and their meat offring, and their drink offrings: and powre thereby all the blood of the burnt offring, and all the blood of the sacrifice, and the brasen altar shalbe for me to inquire of God.
16.16: And Vriiah the Priest did according to all that King Ahaz had commanded.
16.17: And King Ahaz brake the borders of the bases, and took the caldrons from off them, and took down the sea from the brasen oxen that were under it, and put it upon a pavement of stones.
16.18: And the vail for the Sabbath (that they had made in the house) and the Kings entrie without turned he to the house of the Lord, because of the King of Asshur.
16.19: Concerning the rest of the actes of Ahaz, which he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
16.20: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buryed with his fathers in the citie of David, and Hezekiah his sonne reigned in his stead.

17.1: In the twelft yeere of Ahaz King of Judah began Hoshea the sonne of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel, and reigned nine yeeres.
17.2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the Kinges of Israel, that were before him.
17.3: And Shalmaneser king of Asshur came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.
17.4: And the King of Asshur found treason in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So King of Egypt, and brought no present unto the King of Asshur, as he had done yeerely: therfore the king of Asshur shut him up, and put him in prison.
17.5: Then the king of Asshur came up throughout all the land, and went against Samaria, and besieged it three yeere.
17.6: In the ninth yeere of Hoshea, the King of Asshur took Samaria, and caryed Israel away unto Asshur, and put them in Halah, and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
17.7: For when the children of Israel sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them out of the land of Egypt, from under ye hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and feared other gods,
17.8: And walked according to the facions of the Heathen, whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel, and after the maners of the Kings of Israel, which they used,
17.9: And the children of Israel had done secretly things that were not upright before the Lord their God, and throughout all their cities had built hie places, both from the tower of the watch, to the defensed citie,
17.10: And had made them images and groves upon every hie hill, and under every green tree,
17.11: And there burnt incense in all the hie places, as did the heathen, whom the Lord had taken away before them, and wrought wicked things to anger the Lord,
17.12: And served idoles: whereof the Lord had sayd unto them, Ye shall do no such thing,
17.13: Notwithstanding the Lord testified to Israel, and to Judah by all the Prophets, and by all the Seers, saying, Turn from your evil wayes, and keep my commandements and my statutes, according to all the Law, which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the Prophets.
17.14: Nevertheless they would not obey, but hardened their neckes, like to the neckes of their fathers, that did not beleeue in the Lord their God.
